sourceRefs.locator: Danish Journal of Archaeology 5, pp. 21–25, especially fig. 3 (separate felling dates for Storhaug loose timber, Oseberg hull and burial chamber), table 2 (ring series) and “Narrowing down the location of the shipbuilding site” (beech and probable origins in western Norway).
Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.
“Oppdag skipsgravene” and the map “Kart over Grønhaug og Storhaug på Karmøy,” showing Storhaug north of Grønhaug beside the Karmsund.
Local heritage map of the two burial grounds beside Karmsund, with the Storhaug site on the Gunnarshaug farm to the north.
